title: Grok Bot tutorial
description: Numbered tutorials on Grok Bot, from the desktop app and the shared computer through the phone.
heroAlt: A cream paper laptop, a steel-blue desktop monitor and a small standing phone sit on a torn sand blotter, with a wavy coral cord running in front of them, against layered deep-navy paper and a small pine in the corner.

title: AI image models
description: Image models, one or two per part, answered on the same questions from each vendor's own pages.
heroAlt: A slate paper easel holds a torn-paper mountain scene under a coral sun, flanked by stacked empty frames and ochre, rust and cream paper scraps on a wooden table against a kraft-paper wall.

title: AI movie models
description: Video models, one or two per part, answered on the same questions from each vendor's own pages.
heroAlt: A slate paper film projector casts a sulfur-yellow beam onto a three-frame film strip with a coral middle frame, beside a rusty-red clapper, on layered deep-navy paper with rust and sand tears.

title: AI voice models
description: Voice models, one or two per part, answered on the same questions from each vendor's own pages.

title: Vectors, Plainly
description: What a vector database does, in six parts: the idea, the index, tenancy, retrieval quality, RAG, and production.
heroAlt: A coral paper disc at the centre is tied by short cream strings to two clusters of slate-blue dots on a torn map of navy and sand paper, with smaller quiet clusters around them.

title: Kubernetes from Zero
description: Kubernetes from the first container to a production cluster, one part a day.
heroAlt: Paper-cut wooden-brown ship's helm behind a slate-blue control-plane tray with a cream manifest and four modules, worker nodes with cream and coral crates on a navy cluster map and a coral return loop
audience: People starting with Kubernetes: a junior DevOps engineer, a developer who deploys their own service, or anyone who has run docker run and wants the next step.
learns: What problem Kubernetes solves, and what desired state means.
How to start a cluster on a laptop and follow one kubectl apply through the control plane.
The path from a first container toward a production cluster, one part at a time.

title: Containers from Zero
description: A ten-lesson foundation in Docker and Compose, from what a container is to a small web app with a database on one machine, one lesson a week.
audience: People new to containers: a developer who wants to run their app the same way everywhere, a student, or an operator who has seen docker run in a README and wants to understand it.
learns: What a container is, how it differs from a virtual machine, and how to build an image with a Dockerfile.
How to run containers with ports, volumes, networks and configuration, then describe them in one Compose file.
How to run a small web app with a database, read health checks, restart policies and logs when it fails, and clean up.
lessonTime: about 15 minutes of reading, plus an optional lab
